title: AI forgets the middle too
caption: A long AI chat has the same shape as the call: the first and the newest messages get used, the middle gets lost, and a detail that keeps coming back survives.

left.1: Yes! But first, did you hear about Mum’s new phone?
left.3: She sent me forty photos of her thumb.
left.4: Ha! Did you see the neighbours’ renovation?
left.5: Don’t get me started. And my back hurts again.
left.6: And Pepper ate a whole birthday cake, candles included!
left.8: Not yet. Oh, dinner is ready, I have to run.

right.m3: Plan a summer party for our team: 40 people, end of June, budget <budget>40,000 euro</budget>.
right.m4: Happy to help! Indoor or outdoor? Any dietary needs I should know about?
right.m9: Three options: Quinta terrace, LX Factory rooftop, Estrela garden pavilion.
right.m10: The catering offers are in the project folder. Which one fits?
right.m13: Check hotels near the venue for 15 guests from abroad.
right.m15: Hotel Lumen and Casa do Rio both have 15 rooms free on 27 June.
right.m22: Great, put the full plan together.
right.m24: Full plan: venue <cost>14,800</cost>, catering with the vegetarian menu <cost>21,600</cost>, hotels <cost>9,400</cost>, music <cost>6,500</cost>. Total <budget>52,300 euro</budget>.

standoutNote: Said four times, so a fresh copy is always near the end.
overBudget: 12,300 over the budget from the first message
bottomLine: <muted>With your sister, a lost detail is funny.</muted> With a deadline, it’s expensive.
studyNote: <planted>Measured by planting a fact in a long input, not in today’s chat apps</planted> · <varies>how deep the middle dips varies</varies>

measured-even-for-long-input-models.description: Relevant information is used best at the beginning or end of the input and worst in the middle, also in models built for long contexts [1].

liu-lost-in-the-middle.title: Liu et al., Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

a-built-in-pull-to-the-start.header: A built-in pull to the start
a-built-in-pull-to-the-start.description: The first tokens of an input draw strong attention as an "attention sink", even when they carry no meaning [1].

xiao-attention-sinks.title: Xiao et al., Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks

two-position-effects.description: Causal masking biases attention toward earlier positions, and relative position encodings favour nearby tokens, which trades off against the accumulating importance of early positions [1]; that these two together produce the middle dip is an inference, the paper's abstract does not state it.

wu-position-bias.title: Wu et al., On the Emergence of Position Bias in Transformers

the-strength-varies.description: The dip is strongest when the input fills up to about half the window; beyond that the start advantage fades and the end advantage stays [1].

veseli-positional-biases-shift.title: Veseli et al., Positional Biases Shift as Inputs Approach Context Window Limits

planted-facts-not-chat-products.description: The studies plant a fact in the input and test whether the model retrieves it; none tests current chat products, so applying them to a chat is an inference [1].

liu-lost-in-the-middle.title: Liu et al., Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

meet-the-summer-party-chat.title: Meet the summer-party chat
meet-the-summer-party-chat.script: So let me introduce a chat that stays with us for the rest of the episode. You plan a company summer party with an AI: 40 people, end of June, a budget of 40,000 euro, and you give it a catering PDF and a guest list. Remember this chat, because we come back to it on every slide that follows.

it-happens-in-a-long-chat-too.title: It happens in a long chat too
it-happens-in-a-long-chat-too.script: Now let it run for an hour. You started with the plan and the budget, and the first messages tend to get used, the latest messages tend to get used, and the middle gets lost. A detail you keep repeating, like the 12 vegetarian guests, survives. Later the budget slips, which is odd for a number from your very first message, and why that happens comes on a later slide.

a-shape-not-a-brain.title: A shape, not a brain
a-shape-not-a-brain.script: I'm not saying the AI thinks the way you do. It has no sister and no Mum with a new phone. What I'm saying is that the shape is the same, and a shape is something you can predict, so you know where to expect the slip.

what-a-lost-detail-costs.title: What a lost detail costs
what-a-lost-detail-costs.script: With your sister, a lost detail is funny. With a deadline, it's expensive. So ask yourself which one your chat is: the one with the dog and the cake, or the one with your budget in it.
